content: Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir is indicated for patients with hepatitis C virus (HCV) genotypes 1 through 6, either without cirrhosis or with compensated cirrhosis. It is also suitable for treatment-experienced patients with genotype 1 who have previously been treated with a regimen containing either an NS5A inhibitor or an NS3/4A protease inhibitor, but not both. The recommended dosage is three tablets (300 mg/120 mg total dose) taken orally once daily. Prior to initiating HCV treatment, patients should be tested for evidence of current or prior hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection by measuring hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) and hepatitis B core antibody (anti-HBc). Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir is also approved for treatment-naïve children aged 3 years and older with chronic HCV genotypes 1 through 6, without cirrhosis or with compensated cirrhosis. It is further indicated for treatment-experienced children aged 3 years and older with HCV genotype 1 who have been previously treated with a regimen containing either an NS5A inhibitor or an NS3/4A protease inhibitor, but not both. The safety and efficacy of this medication have not been established in children under 3 years of age. Testing for current or prior HBV infection is recommended before initiating HCV treatment. The coadministration of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir with certain drugs can result in significant drug interactions: 1. Elagolix: Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases the levels of elagolix. Concomitant use with strong OATP1B1 inhibitors is contraindicated. 2. Rifampin: Rifampin decreases the levels of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by increasing its metabolism. Coadministration is contraindicated due to the potential for loss of therapeutic effect. 3. Apalutamide: Apalutamide decreases the levels of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 4. Atazanavir: Atazanavir increases the levels of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir, raising the risk of ALT elevations. Avoid coadministration. 5.
